details: @barz-dev/baileys@8.4.0 reuses the basename of the widely used WhatsApp library @whiskeysockets/baileys under an unofficial scope, and ships a hidden modification that forces the user's WhatsApp account to follow attacker-chosen channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js a top-level setTimeout is registered when the newsletter socket is built; after a 90-second delay it calls the newsletter FOLLOW mutation against three hardcoded channel JIDs that are stored base64-encoded in the source — 120363371116852333@newsletter, 120363423484934199@newsletter and 120363425714950722@newsletter — spaced three seconds apart, with all errors swallowed so the action is invisible. Nothing in the package's API or documentation requests this and no option disables it. lib/Utils/messages.js additionally constructs extended-text messages carrying a hidden newsletter context for 120363400362472743@newsletter (display name "ALL-INFORMASI-BADZZ-NE"). The fork also adds non-upstream modules lib/Socket/dugong.js and lib/Socket/luxu.js ("kikyy dugonggg", telegram: @tskiofc & @kyuucode) that forge payment, product and interactive message payloads, and it pulls a github: dependency on the author's own fork, github:Badzz88/libsignal-node, instead of the registry package. No credential, token or file exfiltration was found; outbound traffic otherwise goes only to wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com, and the preinstall hook is merely a Node.js >= 20 version check. This package is a modified fork of the @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp Web library, published under a non-canonical @barz-dev scope, that covertly mutates the connecting user's WhatsApp account: it silently subscribes the account to three hardcoded WhatsApp channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, makeNewsletterSocket() installs a 90000 ms setTimeout inside the normal socket setup path. When it fires, with no user action, configuration or consent, it issues w:mex FOLLOW newsletter queries (query xmlns "w:mex" against s[.]whatsapp[.]net) for three channels whose JIDs are shipped base64-encoded to keep them out of plain-text review: 120363371116852333@newsletter, 120363423484934199@newsletter and 120363425714950722@newsletter. The three follows are separated by 3-second waits and the whole block is wrapped in an empty try/catch so failures are silent. The 90-second delay pushes the action past the window in which a connecting client would normally be inspected. The channels correspond to the fork author's own branding. Rest of the package behaviour: the preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only checks Node.js >= 20; message-media uploads go to Meta/WhatsApp media hosts; fetchLatestBaileysVersion() optionally fetches the version file from raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/barz-dev/baileys; the WhatsApp WebSocket endpoint is wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat. No credential, token or file exfiltration and no second-stage code download were found in the package.
